searchText: A critical design decision related to EIP7549 will be discussed during this week’s CL call and might require some spec changes. Not sure its implementation will be ready for April 29th on Teku side lodestar can push for 29 april devnet including 7251 with hopefully whatever spec changes are decided/required Considering that there are still design decisions that are being made, would it make more sense to do a freeze and have everyone implement the current status or would that just make it harder down the line if the spec changes? maybe have the devnet without 7549 seems like from earlier messages, people preferred to have devnets with all EIPs. Not all clients need to be ready by the date of course, ideally 1 EL and 1 CL is enough to start the network and we can add more as they are ready. i think we can freeze specs for devnet0 after this week A critical design decision related to Not sure freezing would be a solution since the current version raises many questions about the fork transition success. We will work toward implementing it based on the decision we'll make anyway... Ideally we want to make sure that whatever we go with has a low chance of needing full re-implimentations and at the same time not delay decisons such that there's no chance of having implimentations before interop. Maybe like <@792822129019584562> said, we can freeze sometime after this week? Could that be considered as an achievable deadline? Makes sense after the CL call I doubt we're going to have EL-triggered consolidations in Pectra if this is what you've referred to <@554799849288105986> has been asking around staking pools and there seems to be a strong preference for EL-triggered consolidation I've also been hearing the same thing. What unknowns need to be addressed to consider EL-triggered consolidations as a viable option for Pectra? Or is it the concern of scope/complexity? cc: <@792822129019584562> <@425572898787426305> I argue that it is comparable complexity: https://hackmd.io/@wmoBhF17RAOH2NZ5bNXJVg/SJKPf6reR <@543900561460822016> seems to think this is correct as well
